Chapter 1: Some basic concepts of chemistry

sections.heading: A counting unit
sections.text: A **mole** is a counting unit, like a dozen. One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles: this is **Avogadro's number**.

sections.heading: Why so big?
sections.text: Atoms are tiny, so we need a huge number of them to make an amount we can weigh.

misconceptions.1: 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s is the speed of light.

questions.stem: How many molecules are in 0.5 mol of CO₂?
A mole is best described as…
questions.explanation: Like a dozen, it counts particles.

misconceptions.0: Molar mass is a mass; the mole is a count.

questions.stem: 1 mol of Na and 1 mol of Cl contain…
questions.explanation: One mole of anything has 6.022 × 10²³ particles.

misconceptions.2: Their masses differ (23 g vs 35.5 g).

Chapter 1: Some basic concepts of chemistry

sections.heading: Molar mass
sections.text: The **molar mass** is the mass of one mole, in g/mol. Add the atomic masses: H₂O = 2 × 1 + 16 = 18 g/mol.

sections.heading: Grams to moles
sections.text: moles = mass ÷ molar mass. 36 g of water = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 mol.

questions.stem: How many moles are in 58.5 g of NaCl (Na = 23, Cl = 35.5)?
